::: {.callout-note icon="true"}
## Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

- organize the pipeline sections in their required execution order;
- distinguish configuration, functions, processing, analysis, and outputs;
- verify that the complete script can be parsed by R;
- run the pipeline from a clean R session;
- capture execution time and failure information;
- confirm that the source catalog is valid;
- verify that all primary and supplementary source roles are preserved;
- confirm that all four figures are generated;
- create a final pipeline-run summary;
- distinguish running the R pipeline from rendering the Quarto website.
:::

## What this lesson accomplishes

In Lessons 1–17, you built the pipeline incrementally.

You now have code that:

1. prepares the project;
2. loads packages;
3. validates the source catalog;
4. downloads the NHANES source files;
5. imports and inspects every XPT file;
6. investigates the 2001–2002 second CBC examination;
7. combines the primary CBC files;
8. combines the Demographic files;
9. merges the two components;
10. validates the merged dataset;
11. creates readable labels;
12. saves reusable outputs;
13. analyzes hemoglobin;
14. creates four professional figures.

Lesson 18 does not introduce a new analytical method.

It organizes the completed work into a reproducible execution sequence.

## The final pipeline file

The complete script should be stored as:

```text
nhanes_pipeline.R
```

at the root of the project.

Your project should contain:

```text
NHANES/
├── nhanes_pipeline.R
├── config/
├── data/
├── outputs/
├── R/
├── tutorial/
├── _quarto.yml
└── styles.css
```

## Pipeline execution order

The sections in `nhanes_pipeline.R` should appear in this order:

```text
Section 1: Project setup
Section 2: Package validation and loading
Section 3: Output-directory creation
Section 4: Source-catalog definition and validation
Section 5: Download one test file
Section 6: Download all source files
Section 7: Inspect all downloaded files
Section 8: Investigate and handle duplicate records
Section 9: Combine files within each component
Section 10: Merge CBC and Demographic data
Section 11: Validate the merged analytical dataset
Section 12: Create readable variable labels
Section 13: Save reusable outputs
Section 14: Analyze and prepare hemoglobin data
Section 15: Create professional hemoglobin figures
Section 16: Complete pipeline-run validation
```

::: {.callout-important icon="true"}
## Execution order matters

Later sections depend on objects created earlier.

For example:

- file inspection requires the acquisition manifest;
- duplicate handling requires imported source objects;
- component combination requires the duplicate policy;
- merging requires validated component datasets;
- plotting requires the Lesson 16 summary datasets.

Do not rearrange sections casually.
:::

## Add the final pipeline-validation section

At the bottom of `nhanes_pipeline.R`, add:

```r
# ============================================================
# SECTION 16: COMPLETE PIPELINE-RUN VALIDATION
# ============================================================
```

## Record pipeline start time

Ideally, the pipeline start time should be recorded near the beginning of the script.

Near the top of `nhanes_pipeline.R`, add:

```r
pipeline_started_at <- Sys.time()
```

At the end of the script, calculate the finish time:

```r
pipeline_finished_at <- Sys.time()
```

Calculate elapsed time:

```r
pipeline_elapsed_seconds <- as.numeric(
  difftime(
    pipeline_finished_at,
    pipeline_started_at,
    units = "secs"
  )
)
```

## Define critical final objects

Create a list of objects that must exist after a successful run:

```r
required_pipeline_objects <- c(
  "nhanes_catalog",
  "acquisition_manifest",
  "source_inspection_report",
  "imported_sources",
  "cbc_second_exam_2001_2002",
  "primary_cbc_sources",
  "primary_demographic_sources",
  "cbc_primary_1999_2018",
  "demographics_1999_2018",
  "cbc_demographics_1999_2018",
  "cbc_demographics_validated",
  "cbc_demographics_labelled",
  "cbc_demographics_analysis",
  "hemoglobin_complete_cases",
  "hemoglobin_trend_figure_data",
  "hemoglobin_distribution_figure_data",
  "hemoglobin_record_count_figure_data",
  "hemoglobin_missingness_figure_data",
  "hemoglobin_trend_plot",
  "hemoglobin_distribution_plot",
  "hemoglobin_record_count_plot",
  "hemoglobin_missingness_plot"
)
```

Check whether each object exists:

```r
pipeline_object_check <- tibble::tibble(
  object = required_pipeline_objects,
  exists = purrr::map_lgl(
    required_pipeline_objects,
    exists
  )
)
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  pipeline_object_check,
  n = Inf
)
```

Identify missing objects:

```r
missing_pipeline_objects <-
  pipeline_object_check |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !exists
  )
```

Stop when required objects are missing:

```r
if (
  nrow(
    missing_pipeline_objects
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The completed pipeline is missing required objects: ",
    paste(
      missing_pipeline_objects$object,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

## Validate the source catalog

The production catalog requires these columns:

```r
required_final_catalog_columns <- c(
  "dataset_id",
  "cycle",
  "cycle_start",
  "cycle_end",
  "component",
  "file_id",
  "exam",
  "analysis_role",
  "record_level",
  "merge_key",
  "expected_rows",
  "url"
)
```

Identify missing catalog columns:

```r
missing_final_catalog_columns <- setdiff(
  required_final_catalog_columns,
  names(
    nhanes_catalog
  )
)
```

Stop if any are missing:

```r
if (
  length(
    missing_final_catalog_columns
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The final source catalog is missing required columns: ",
    paste(
      missing_final_catalog_columns,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

Check unique dataset identifiers:

```r
if (
  anyDuplicated(
    nhanes_catalog$dataset_id
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The final source catalog contains duplicated dataset_id values."
  )
}
```

Check analytical roles:

```r
supported_analysis_roles <- c(
  "primary",
  "supplementary"
)
```

```r
unsupported_analysis_roles <- setdiff(
  unique(
    nhanes_catalog$analysis_role
  ),
  supported_analysis_roles
)
```

Stop if unsupported roles exist:

```r
if (
  length(
    unsupported_analysis_roles
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "Unsupported analytical roles were found: ",
    paste(
      unsupported_analysis_roles,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

## Validate source-file counts

The completed catalog should contain:

```text
10 primary CBC files
1 supplementary second-examination CBC file
10 primary Demographic files
```

Create a summary:

```r
final_catalog_role_summary <-
  nhanes_catalog |>
  dplyr::count(
    component,
    analysis_role,
    name = "source_files"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    component,
    analysis_role
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  final_catalog_role_summary,
  n = Inf
)
```

Count primary CBC files:

```r
final_primary_cbc_count <-
  nhanes_catalog |>
  dplyr::filter(
    component == "cbc",
    analysis_role == "primary"
  ) |>
  nrow()
```

Count supplementary CBC files:

```r
final_supplementary_cbc_count <-
  nhanes_catalog |>
  dplyr::filter(
    component == "cbc",
    analysis_role == "supplementary"
  ) |>
  nrow()
```

Count primary Demographic files:

```r
final_primary_demographic_count <-
  nhanes_catalog |>
  dplyr::filter(
    component == "demographic",
    analysis_role == "primary"
  ) |>
  nrow()
```

Validate:

```r
if (
  final_primary_cbc_count != 10
) {
  stop(
    "The final catalog does not contain 10 primary CBC files."
  )
}
```

```r
if (
  final_supplementary_cbc_count != 1
) {
  stop(
    "The final catalog does not contain exactly one supplementary CBC file."
  )
}
```

```r
if (
  final_primary_demographic_count != 10
) {
  stop(
    "The final catalog does not contain 10 primary Demographic files."
  )
}
```

## Confirm the second examination policy

Confirm that the supplementary source is identified:

```r
final_supplementary_cbc_sources <-
  nhanes_catalog |>
  dplyr::filter(
    component == "cbc",
    analysis_role == "supplementary"
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    dataset_id,
    cycle,
    file_id,
    exam,
    analysis_role
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  final_supplementary_cbc_sources,
  n = Inf
)
```

Confirm that `L25_2_B` remains excluded from the primary stack:

```r
second_exam_in_primary_stack <-
  "L25_2_B" %in%
    unique(
      cbc_primary_1999_2018$source_file_id
    )
```

Expected:

```text
[1] FALSE
```

Stop if it entered the primary stack:

```r
if (
  second_exam_in_primary_stack
) {
  stop(
    "L25_2_B was incorrectly included in the primary CBC stack."
  )
}
```

Confirm that the supplementary object contains records:

```r

  nrow(
    cbc_second_exam_2001_2002
  ) < 1
) {
  stop(
    "The preserved second-examination dataset contains no records."
  )
}
```

## Validate survey-cycle coverage

Define:

```r
final_expected_cycles <- c(
  "1999-2000",
  "2001-2002",
  "2003-2004",
  "2005-2006",
  "2007-2008",
  "2009-2010",
  "2011-2012",
  "2013-2014",
  "2015-2016",
  "2017-2018"
)
```

Identify observed cycles:

```r
final_observed_cycles <- sort(
  unique(
    cbc_demographics_labelled$survey_cycle
  )
)
```

Find missing cycles:

```r
final_missing_cycles <- setdiff(
  final_expected_cycles,
  final_observed_cycles
)
```

Find unexpected cycles:

```r
final_unexpected_cycles <- setdiff(
  final_observed_cycles,
  final_expected_cycles
)
```

Stop if missing:

```r
if (
  length(
    final_missing_cycles
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The completed dataset is missing survey cycles: ",
    paste(
      final_missing_cycles,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

Stop if unexpected cycles appear:

```r
if (
  length(
    final_unexpected_cycles
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "The completed dataset contains unexpected survey cycles: ",
    paste(
      final_unexpected_cycles,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

## Create the final validation table

Run:

```r
complete_pipeline_validation <-
  tibble::tibble(
    check = c(
      "All required pipeline objects exist",
      "Catalog contains required columns",
      "Catalog dataset identifiers are unique",
      "Catalog analytical roles are supported",
      "Ten primary CBC sources are declared",
      "One supplementary CBC source is declared",
      "Ten primary Demographic sources are declared",
      "Second CBC examination is excluded from primary stack",
      "Second CBC examination is preserved separately",
      "All primary acquisitions succeeded",
      "Final key values are complete",
      "Final composite key is unique",
      "All ten expected cycles are present",
      "No unexpected cycles are present",
      "All four figure objects are valid",
      "All twelve exported figure files exist",
      "All exported figure files are nonempty",
      "All required processed datasets exist",
      "All required processed datasets are nonempty"
    ),
    passed = c(
      nrow(
        missing_pipeline_objects
      ) == 0,
      length(
        missing_final_catalog_columns
      ) == 0,
      anyDuplicated(
        nhanes_catalog$dataset_id
      ) == 0,
      length(
        unsupported_analysis_roles
      ) == 0,
      final_primary_cbc_count == 10,
      final_supplementary_cbc_count == 1,
      final_primary_demographic_count == 10,
      !second_exam_in_primary_stack,
      nrow(
        cbc_second_exam_2001_2002
      ) > 0,
      nrow(
        failed_primary_acquisitions
      ) == 0,
      nrow(
        final_pipeline_missing_keys
      ) == 0,
      nrow(
        final_pipeline_duplicate_keys
      ) == 0,
      length(
        final_missing_cycles
      ) == 0,
      length(
        final_unexpected_cycles
      ) == 0,
      all(
        final_figure_object_check$is_ggplot
      ),
      all(
        final_figure_file_check$exists
      ),
      all(
        final_figure_file_check$size_bytes > 0
      ),
      all(
        final_dataset_file_check$exists
      ),
      all(
        final_dataset_file_check$size_bytes > 0
      )
    )
  )
```

Inspect:

```r
print(
  complete_pipeline_validation,
  n = Inf
)
```

Identify failures:

```r
failed_complete_pipeline_checks <-
  complete_pipeline_validation |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !passed
  )
```

Stop if a check fails:

```r
if (
  nrow(
    failed_complete_pipeline_checks
  ) > 0
) {
  stop(
    "Complete pipeline validation failed: ",
    paste(
      failed_complete_pipeline_checks$check,
      collapse = ", "
    )
  )
}
```

```r
complete_pipeline_run_summary <-
  tibble::tibble(
    metric = c(
      "Pipeline started",

      "Supplementary CBC source files",

    value = c(
      format(

    scales::comma(
      nrow(
        cbc_demographics_labelled
      )
    )
  )
)

message(
  "Four professional figures were generated in PNG, PDF, and SVG formats."
)
```

# Check the script before running it

## Save the file

In VS Code, open:

```text
nhanes_pipeline.R
```

Press:

```text
Command + S
```

## Check whether R can parse the script

Open the terminal at the project root and run:

```bash
Rscript -e 'parse(file = "nhanes_pipeline.R"); cat("Script parsed successfully.\n")'
```

A successful result ends with:

```text
Script parsed successfully.
```

A parsing failure means the script contains a structural syntax problem such as:

- a missing parenthesis;
- a missing brace;
- an incomplete quotation mark;
- a malformed operator;
- an unfinished function;
- a copied Markdown fence inside the R script.

::: {.callout-warning icon="true"}
## Parsing does not run the pipeline

This command checks the script’s R syntax.

It does not:

- download files;
- process data;
- create datasets;
- generate figures.
:::

# Run from a clean R session

## Why use a clean session?

A script can appear to work because objects from previous interactive work remain in memory.

A reproducible pipeline must create every required object itself.

Using `Rscript` starts a separate R process and reduces dependence on the current VS Code session.

## Run the complete pipeline

From the project root, run:

```bash
Rscript nhanes_pipeline.R
```

Leave the terminal open while it runs.

The script may take time because it can:

- validate packages;
- download source files;
- import multiple XPT files;
- create hashes;
- write large processed datasets;
- export twelve figure files;
- produce validation reports.

## Save the console output to a log

For a reproducible execution log, run:

```bash
Rscript nhanes_pipeline.R 2>&1 | tee outputs/validation/complete_pipeline_console.log
```

This displays the output in the terminal and saves it as:

```text
outputs/validation/complete_pipeline_console.log
```

## Check the exit status

Immediately after the pipeline finishes, run:

```bash
echo $?
```

Expected:

```text
0
```

An exit status of `0` means the R process completed without an unhandled error.

A nonzero status means the run failed.

## Do not run the entire script repeatedly while debugging

When an error occurs:

1. read the first error message;
2. identify the section named in the message;
3. inspect the relevant object or file;
4. fix the underlying problem;
5. restart from a clean session;
6. run the complete script again.

Avoid repeatedly executing later sections against partially created objects.

# Figures embedded in Lesson 17

Lesson 17 includes the exported PNG figures directly beneath their corresponding creation and export sections.

After the R pipeline successfully generates the figures, Quarto will be able to embed:

```text
Figure 1 under the mean-trend section
Figure 2 under the distribution section
Figure 3 under the record-count section
Figure 4 under the missingness section
```

The R pipeline must generate the PNG files before the website is rendered.

::: {.callout-important icon="true"}
## Run the R pipeline before rendering the website

The correct order is:

```text
1. Run nhanes_pipeline.R
2. Confirm that all four PNG files exist
3. Render the Quarto website
```

If the PNG files do not exist, Lesson 17 cannot display them.
:::

# Running the pipeline is not rendering the website

These are separate tasks.

## Run the analytical pipeline

```bash
Rscript nhanes_pipeline.R
```

This creates:

- processed datasets;
- tables;
- validation reports;
- figures.

## Render the Quarto website

```bash
quarto render
```

This creates the HTML website.

We are **not** running `quarto render` yet because Lessons 19 and 20 still need to be finalized.

# Optional: create a dedicated runner script

You can create:

```text
run_pipeline.R
```

with:

```r
pipeline_script <- "nhanes_pipeline.R"

if (
  !file.exists(
    pipeline_script
  )
) {
  stop(
    "Pipeline script does not exist: ",
    pipeline_script
  )
}

message(
  "Starting the NHANES pipeline."
)

source(
  pipeline_script,
  echo = FALSE,
  chdir = FALSE
)

message(
  "The NHANES pipeline finished."
)
```

Then run:

```bash
Rscript run_pipeline.R
```

This is optional.

The main reproducible command remains:

```bash
Rscript nhanes_pipeline.R
```

# Common assembly problems

## Code appears in the wrong order

An object is used before it is created.

Review the section order at the beginning of this lesson.

## Markdown fences were copied into the R script

The R file must not contain lines such as:

```r
